messages:
Rafael (AE): HealthSpan POC is blocked. They get 401 + 'scope_mismatch' calling /v1/generate from their CI job.
Mina (solutions): thanks — ask for the exact curl or SDK call and the raw response body + headers. Also ask them to confirm which key they used (redact).
Customer: here's the SDK call (redacted): `rw_client.generate(api_key='sk-hs-OLD', model='redwood-small', prompt='test')` Response: {"error":"scope_mismatch", "request_id":"rq_hs_77"} Headers: `x-rw-auth: failed`, `x-rw-org: healthspan-prod`
Devon (eng): two quick things: 1) run GET /v1/keys/inspect with same Authorization header to see owner_org/owner_project/scopes; 2) check for legacy headers. Some older SDKs send `X-Api-Key` and our gateway may treat that differently for scoped keys.
Customer: ran inspect -> `owner_org: healthspan-stage`, `owner_project: onboard-ci`, `scopes: ["embeddings:read"]`
Rafael (AE): looks like the key was created in their staging org and only has embeddings scope. That explains the mismatch.
Customer: odd — we created a new key in the console under the correct project though. Could be a CI cache of an old secret?
Clara (support): check where the key is stored in CI. Many teams stash a value in two places and one job still uses the old secret. Also confirm the SDK version — older rw-client v0.8 used `X-Api-Key` header without binding metadata.
Customer: our CI uses a secrets manager and injects `API_KEY` into env. The job log shows `sk-hs-NEW` but inspect shows old owner. Could there be propagation delay?
Devon (eng): possible. When you create a new key there can be an auth cache propagation window (~20-60s). If the old key was swapped very quickly you might see mixed results. Also, if the job uses the SDK and the SDK sets an explicit `x-rw-org` header from config, that can cause an org mismatch even if the token is correct.
Mina (solutions): can you paste the raw request headers from the failing run (redact key)? We're looking for any `X-Api-Key`, `Authorization`, or `x-rw-org` headers.
Customer: headers from failing run: `Authorization: Bearer sk-hs-NEW`, `x-rw-org: healthspan-stage`
Rafael (AE): aha — the token is for prod but the header `x-rw-org` points to stage. Gateway rejects since token owner_org != header org -> scope_mismatch.
Customer: where is x-rw-org coming from? we didn't set it in our env.
Clara (support): many SDKs will add `x-rw-org` from client config or from a previous env var. Check your rw-client config and CI environment variables for `RW_ORG` or similar. Also check that the job runner doesn't add request metadata.
Customer: found RW_ORG env var in CI set to healthspan-stage. Removed it, retried immediately -> still got 401 with `request_id: rq_hs_78` and header `x-rw-auth: pending-propagation`.
Devon (eng): pending-propagation indicates new key still propagating through our auth caches. Wait ~45s and retry. If you still hit 401, send the `request_id` and we'll pull the trace.
Customer: waited 60s and retried -> 200 OK, model tokens returned. Thanks! Quick follow-ups: can you recommend best practice for CI POCs to avoid this?
Mina (solutions): checklist we give customers: 1) Use keys created in the correct project/org; 2) Use least-privilege scopes (inference:invoke for generate/chat); 3) Avoid hardcoding RW_ORG unless necessary — prefer inferring from key; 4) When rotating keys, wait ~1m before heavy test runs; 5) Set project spend cap for POC.
Rafael (AE): I'll send that checklist and a short note for the security questionnaire (scoped short-lived keys, IP allowlist for CI runners if possible).
AuthBot: Tip: To inspect binding: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/inspect` -> returns owner_org, owner_project, scopes.
Clara (support): if you hit any further 401s, include `request_id` and the `x-rw-*` headers. We can trace quickly.
Customer: implemented changes, all green in CI now. Appreciate the quick help.
Rafael (AE): closing the POC blocker. Thanks team! :white_check_mark:
